answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation: every agent locks a refundable copper-grade deposit before it can trade, cheap for one honest identity but ruinous at scale. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a dune building grain by grain, and only long-lived agents with a clean history earn full trust. New identities start in a low-trust meadow of capped transactions, so an attacker must fund thousands of deposits and wait months to mimic a single established agent, a cost that dwarfs the profit of one fake identity.
